intent: Put running text, a label, a meta line or a mono path on one of the kit's type ramp roles, in the default or the muted tone.
typical_uses: A muted meta line such as an update time, or a key figure in the kpi role
A file path or a command name in the mono role

dont_use_when.situation: A block of code with a copy action
The description line of a Card

invariants.text: Each typography value sets font size, line height, weight and tracking from the matching `--text-<role>-*` ramp tokens; `mono` also sets `--font-mono`, and `kpi` and `kpi-lg` set tabular figures. The tone sets only `color`, from `--foreground` or `--muted-foreground`.
The text has zero margin on whatever element `render` substitutes.
An explicit `typography={null}` or `tone={null}` resolves to body and default.

anti_patterns.dont: Set a font size or a colour on Text from outside
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pick the ramp role with `typography` and the colour with `tone`

anti_patterns.dont: Use the micro or meta role for a paragraph of running text
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep running text on the body role; meta and micro are for short lines

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (Text passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is for the element, such as `render={<span />}` inside a row or `render={<code />}` for a path.

bad.title: A tone guessed from StatusDot
bad.why: Text has two tones, default and muted; a state colour belongs to StatusDot or Badge.

companions.typed_by: cva(...), returns (props: VariantProps<typeof textVariants> & { className?: string }) => string
companions.description: The typography and tone class-name builder Text itself uses, exported beside the component.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, {}> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (Text passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is for the element, such as `render={<span />}` inside a row or `render={<code />}` for a path.
